key_insight: Active learning makes interatomic-potential training more data-efficient by selecting new reference calculations for configurations relevant to intended simulations.
engineering_relevance: Adaptive training can help tailor atomistic models to operating conditions in mechanics, diffusion, functional materials, and reactive chemistry.
method: Generate candidate configurations and select informative samples.
Run reference calculations, update the potential, and repeat.
Use committee, Gaussian-process, pretrained-representation, or reaction-aware selection strategies.
evidence_signal: The review surveys more than 70 studies, emphasizing 2020–2026, across diverse methods and applications rather than reporting a single standardized benchmark.
watch_item: Uncertainty estimates are architecture-dependent and can be least reliable in the unfamiliar configurations where trustworthy acquisition is most important.
paper_title: Active Learning for Interatomic Potentials: A Review of Uncertainty-Driven Data Efficiency
